name: Tensile strength and density of T1000 carbon fibre and beryllium-copper

source.located: Maker data sheets: Toray 'TORAYCA T1000G' data sheet (toraycma.com/wp-content/uploads/T1000G-Data-Sheet_02.16.2024.pdf); Materion 'Alloy 25 (C17200)' strip / rod-and-bar data sheets. M could not obtain them. This stage searched for sources that CITE them and read three arXiv papers that tabulate the materials, none of which cites either data sheet.

published_statement: The data-sheet values themselves are NOT READ (egress-blocked; no citing source found). What was READ, verbatim: (1) arXiv:2202.09783 p. 3, 'Table I Comparison of different rotor materials [13]' with rows 'Materials Density (kg/m3) Tensile strength (MPa) ...' and 'Carbon T1000 1520 1950 350 101.8 3.47', [13] = 'B. Bolund, H. Bernhoff, M. Leijon, Flywheel energy and power storage systems, Renewable and Sustainable Energy Reviews. 11 (2007) 235-258' -- a rotor-material (composite) row, not the fibre data sheet; the same paper writes 'E/m = K sigma/rho (2) where K is the shape factor'. (2) arXiv:2005.04976 Table 2 (measured, Cu-2 wt.% Be): 'CG ... 325oC for 10 hours 1170 1280 6' (sigma0.2, UTS in MPa, elongation %) and 'HPT ... 275oC 10 hours 1300 1375 4'; Sec. 1 p. 4 citing ASM (Davis 2001): 'a material with a hardness up to 400 HV, which corresponds to a 1100 MPa yield stress'. (3) arXiv:2410.14855 Table 2: 'BeCu 129 1000' (Young's modulus GPa, yield stress MPa), no source given. No read source states a BeCu density. The tree's use (warpfolder.py:224-227): ('carbon fibre T1000', 6.4e9 Pa, 1800 kg/m^3) and ('beryllium-copper', 1.4e9 Pa, 8250 kg/m^3), status ORDER, feeding burst_speed_m_s = sqrt(sigma/rho) (warpfolder.py:328-330) and the selftest's rounded factors [4.2, 19.4] (warpfolder.py:566-567).
published_hypotheses: FIBRE, NOT COMPOSITE: the T1000G figure is the fibre's (impregnated-strand) strength along the fibre axis. It is not a laminate, transverse or biaxial strength. The test standard was not read.
TYPICAL VALUE: data-sheet figures are typical properties, not design allowables. The sheet's wording was not read.
TEMPER-DEPENDENT: BeCu strength depends on temper and form. Peak-aged C17200 is about 1.36-1.38+ GPa and 1/2H (TD02) is 580-690 MPa. Density also moves with age hardening (8.30 vs 8.36 g/cm3).
ROOM-TEMPERATURE, QUASI-STATIC, ULTIMATE strengths, with no fatigue and no safety factor. This was not read here.
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED (geometry) at warpfolder.py:328-330 ('The classical rotor limit sqrt(sigma/rho), independent of radius') and warpfolder.py:117-118 ('A rotor asked to exceed sqrt(sigma/rho) does not spin; it disassembles'). sqrt(sigma/rho) is exact only for a THIN ROTATING RING (rederive R2: sigma = rho(omega R)^2). A uniform isotropic plane-stress disc peaks at the centre at (3+nu)/8 rho omega^2 R^2 (R3, R3c), so its ceiling is sqrt(8/(3+nu)) sqrt(sigma/rho), which is 1.557x for nu=0.3. A Stodola constant-stress profile satisfies equilibrium (R4), so for an isotropic material there is no fixed-multiple bound, only the taper h(R)/h0 = exp(-(v/v_b)^2/2). The conclusion survives: BeCu is over by 19.4x as a ring, 12.5x as a disc, and needs Stodola taper exp(-189), i.e. a hub > 3e72 m thick for an atom-thick rim (R7). T1000 is over by 4.2x as a ring and 2.7x as a disc. Its Stodola escape (taper 1.2e-4, R7b) is closed only by fibre ANISOTROPY, a hypothesis the tree does not name. The printed 4.2x and 19.4x are RING factors, stated for 'the rotor' without naming the geometry.

NAMED, not drift: the canonical hypothesis 'fibre strength, not a rotor laminate'. The direction was computed: a UD laminate (ORDER inputs Vf=0.6, resin 1200 kg/m^3) has sigma/rho 2.46e6 against the fibre's 3.56e6 (R8), which raises the ring factor from 4.2 to 5.1. Using the fibre figure favours the rotor, so it is conservative.

UNNAMED (grade/temper) at warpfolder.py:226: 'beryllium-copper' names no alloy or temper. 1.4 GPa is peak-aged C17200. Over the band [1.14,1.60] GPa x [8250,8360] kg/m^3 the ring factor is 18.2-21.7. A lower temper only raises it, so this is conservative.
UNNAMED (failure criterion, margin) at warpfolder.py:328-330, 564-570: UTS is compared with one principal stress, with no safety factor, fatigue or temperature. Every omission favours the rotor.

PRECISION, not drift: the selftest pins the ROUNDED factors [4.2, 19.4] (warpfolder.py:566-568), computed from ORDER inputs. The unrounded T1000 factor is 4.2485, 0.0015 below the rounding boundary. With the data-sheet 6,370 MPa it is 4.2585, which prints 4.3 (R5b). BeCu at 1.357-1.38 GPa prints 19.6-19.8. This is a digit discrepancy, not a refutation.

RE-AUDIT, fibre vs composite (READ): the only T1000 figure read this stage is a rotor-composite row, 1950 MPa at 1520 kg/m^3 (2202.09783 Table I via Bolund 2007). It gives a ring factor 7.07 against the tree's 4.25 (reaudit), confirming from a read source the first audit's computed direction: the tree's fibre figure favours the rotor.

RE-AUDIT, BeCu temper (READ): measured peak-aged coarse-grained Cu-2Be UTS 1280 MPa (325 C / 10 h) and nanostructured 1375 MPa give ring factors 20.3 and 19.6 at the tree's 8250 kg/m^3, 1-5% above the tree's 19.4; the tree's 1.4e9 Pa sits at or above the read peak-aged UTS, so it is conservative. Density remains unread.

lacked_data: The exact maker figures (Toray T1000G strength/density/test basis; Materion C17200 temper-by-temper UTS and density) remain unread: every maker host is egress-blocked and no read paper restates them with a citation. The read secondary values (a T1000 composite row; measured peak-aged Cu-2Be UTS) bound the answer on the side that matters: both leave the rotor further over its limit than the tree's ORDER inputs, so the conclusion ROTOR_IS_WITHIN_MATERIAL_LIMITS = False does not depend on the missing sheets. Only the pinned digit (4.2 vs 4.3 at 6,370 MPa, first audit R5b) would need the Toray sheet.
grade_evidence: Unchanged grade, same basis as the first audit: sqrt(sigma/rho) is the thin-ring limit, called 'the classical rotor limit' and applied to 'the rotor' (warpfolder.py:117-118, :328-330); a uniform disc allows sqrt(8/(3+nu)) = 1.557x more and a Stodola profile has no fixed multiple (first audit R2-R4, re-run: 0 failures) -- the solid-disc centre stress (3+nu)/8 rho omega^2 b^2 is also printed in the READ 2202.09783 (p. 10). ROTOR_IS_WITHIN_MATERIAL_LIMITS = False survives on every geometry for BeCu and on ring and disc for T1000. On the data: the maker sheets are still NOT READ (egress-blocked, not routed around) and no citing restatement was found, so the exact published figures stay OPEN; the secondary values that WERE read (T1000 composite 1950 MPa / 1520 kg/m^3; measured peak-aged Cu-2Be 1280-1375 MPa) move the factors to 7.07 and 19.6-20.3, i.e. further over the limit, so the tree's ORDER inputs are conservative.
what_would_change_the_grade: (a) READING the T1000G and Alloy 25 sheets at source: agreement leaves NARROWED with the source READ. Moving the conclusion would need a factor >18 (T1000) or >378 (BeCu) in sigma/rho. (b) The grade could move to STANDS if the owner named, at warpfolder.py:328-330 and 117-118, the thin-ring (or uniform disc with sqrt(8/(3+nu))) geometry and the fibre-anisotropy hypothesis. (c) Evidence that the CAD rotor is a profiled isotropic disc in a material with fibre-level biaxial strength would re-open the T1000 row. (d) The 4.2 -> 4.3 digit is the owner's decision, not repaired here. RE-AUDIT: reading the Toray and Materion sheets (or a paper that quotes them with citation) would settle the pinned digit and the density; it cannot rescue the rotor, since every read value is less favourable than the tree's.
